The change would reach three production call sites in the REST module, plus two test call sites.

**Production callers (confirmed):**

1. **`VisitResource1_9.save(Visit)`** (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/VisitResource1_9.java:251-254`) is the main one. It overrides `DelegatingCrudResource.save` and returns `Context.getVisitService().saveVisit(visit)` directly. Anything that creates or updates a visit through the REST resource goes through this method, so a change to `saveVisit`'s return value, validation, or side effects shows up in the visit POST/update API.
2. **`VisitAttributeResource1_9`** (`.../openmrs1_9/VisitAttributeResource1_9.java`) calls `saveVisit(delegate.getVisit())` at line 114 when a visit attribute is saved, and again at line 126 when one is deleted (voided). Here the visit is saved as a side effect of changing an attribute, so a change to `saveVisit` could affect attribute create/update/delete.

**Tests (confirmed, will need to pass after any change):**

3. `VisitController1_9Test` line 277 calls `service.saveVisit(visit)` in `shouldRemoveAnEncounterFromAnExistingVisitOnEdit`, then relies on the REST edit to remove the encounter.
4. `EncounterController1_9Test` line 359 calls `vs.saveVisit(newVisit)` in `createEncounter_shouldEditVisitPropertyForAnExisitingEncounter`, then checks that the encounter is reassigned to that visit.

**Likely but not verified:**

- The REST controllers that dispatch to `VisitResource1_9.save` (the generic create/update path). I did not trace the call chain from `VisitController1_9` into `DelegatingCrudResource`, so this is an inference from the override.
- `EncounterResource1_9` and other encounter code that changes visit membership. They do not call `saveVisit` directly, so they would only be affected if they depend on the visit being persisted by a path that the change touches. I did not check this.

**Not checked:** I searched only `openmrs-module-webservices.rest` for `saveVisit` references. I did not search other repositories in Falkon (for example `openmrs-module-fhir2`, `openmrs-module-emrapi`, or `openmrs-module-queue`), so they are out of scope for this answer. Reflection-based or string-based dispatch to `saveVisit` would not show up in the symbol search.

**Core declarations (the changed behaviour itself):** `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/VisitService.java:222` (interface), `.../impl/VisitServiceImpl.java:178` (implementation). I did not read the implementation body, so I cannot say what specifically would change.
